reason: A compound of two outline values (rhombic and ovate), like 'linear-lanceolate'; the continuum pattern handles it and no new term is needed.
Puncticulate means finely punctate, and 'glandular' says the dots are glands. That is gland-dotted, a child of PATO punctate.

label: acrodromous
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having two or more primary or strong secondary veins that arise at or above the base and run in convergent arches towards the apex.
reason: A standard venation type (Hickey) with no PATO term. It is a sibling of PATO_0001967 actinodromous and PATO_0001972 reticulodromous. Basal and suprabasal versions are a place on the bearer, not separate terms; FLOPO:0991202 triplinerved is a narrower case.
An insipid fruit lacks flavour, which is exactly PATO flavourless.
Pappose means bearing a pappus. The counts in the examples ('inner 15–20 pappose') are counts of florets and go to the count pattern.
A compound of two values: triangular (deltate) with rounded angles, between rounded and deltate. The continuum pattern handles it, as it does other hyphenated shapes.

reason: The quality is connate (FLOPO:0991067). 'To the middle' says how far the fusion reaches, which is a region of the bearer and not a new value.
A compound of two hair values that both have terms. It goes to the continuum pattern and needs no new term.
Ill-scented means having an unpleasant smell. That is foetid (synonyms: foul-smelling, unpleasant smell).
Lamelliform means shaped like a thin plate or lamella. PATO platelike (exact synonym plate-like) is the existing shape term.

label: bristle-tipped
definition: A pointed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ending in a bristle.
reason: A standard term for teeth and bracts (e.g. oaks). It is a sibling of FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped. It is not aristate, because the tip of a tooth is not an awn.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: depressed FLOPO:0991103 and hemispheroid PATO_0005000)
reason: A hemisphere that is broader than high. Unlike depressed-globose (= oblate), no single term exists, so both existing values are stated.
The examples ('glandular hairs absent', 'dépourvus de poils glanduleux') state that glandular hairs are absent.

target: corolla tube (FLOPO_0985018) on corolla; calyx tube (FLOPO_0986011) on calyx
reason: Not a quality word. It is the tube of the corolla or calyx, measured with length (PATO_0000122); FLOPO already has both tube classes.
Reticulate-veined means net-veined, which is an exact synonym of FLOPO reticulate. 'Not reticulate veined' is its negation.
A compound of two orientation values that both have terms. It is a continuum, not a new term.
'Sub-' plus clavate (claviform = club-shaped). It is handled like 'suborbicular', as the value marked 'approximately'.
Aristiform means awn-like, i.e. very narrow and stiff like a bristle. That matches the definition of setaceous; 'apex aristiform' goes to the apex of the part.
Beak-shaped parts are drawn out into a narrow, beak-like point. That is FLOPO beaked (exact synonym rostrate).
Comb-like is an exact synonym of FLOPO pectinate. The sepal example ('hairs up to 0.8 mm') is a measurement that was matched to the wrong word.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: lacerate FLOPO:0991115 and ciliate PATO_0001408)
reason: A margin that is both irregularly torn and fringed with fine hairs. Two existing values, combined; no new term.
The French equivalent 'en forme de massue' means club-shaped, and a mallet-shaped stigma is thickened at its end. That is PATO clavate.

label: napiform
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a turnip or radish: much thickened in its upper part and abruptly narrowed below.
reason: Napiform is the standard botanical term for taproots of this shape, and PATO has no term for it. It is a sibling of PATO_0005000 hemispheroid.
'Sub-' plus straight means almost straight. It is the approximate-value pattern on PATO straight.
'Without crest' and 'sans crête' negate FLOPO crested. 'Crest' as a part was rejected earlier as a generic part.
A compound of two outline values that both have terms. It goes to the continuum pattern.
Ecalcarate means without a spur, the opposite of calcarate. It applies to flower and corolla. 'Anther bases ecalcarate' has no PO spur class and stays unannotated.
Incanous (incanus) means hoary: covered with fine grey-white hairs. That is FLOPO canescent.
A lanceolate part drawn out into a tail: a compound of two existing values, often stated of the apex. No new term.
